rows.rationale: This revision addresses the reported shallow retention, transit loss, and release-offset problems through deeper nominal contact targeting, short level transfers, basket-relative interior placement, and a retreat before fresh perception. A small exact assignment prioritizes preserving existing groups, while twelve bounded cycles allow more than six objects. Planning alternatives are restricted to explicit zero-execution rejections; uncertain execution stops the policy. Primitive completion and visual heuristics are not treated as proof of grasp or delivery.

This policy addresses the reported failure modes without treating development observations as hidden-state inputs. It changes top-surface grasp targeting to nominal centre-depth targeting, adds bounded stationary gripper settling, separates rim-clearing transport from low release, and removes unconditional destination offsets. Placement candidates remain inside observed basket geometry and account for visible occupants. A small assignment optimizer reduces unnecessary moves, while fresh RGB reassociation and bounded retries support tasks exceeding six objects. Explicit no-path rejections permit limited alternatives; uncertain execution ends the policy without speculative manipulation. These are proposed repairs for independent evaluation, not evidence of task success.

This policy addresses the reported failure modes with additional closed-gripper settling, shorter long-distance transfers, destination hovering followed by a separate release descent, and open settling before retreat. It removes fixed world-frame release offsets and spaces repeated placements within observed basket interiors. A bounded assignment calculation reduces unnecessary transfers, while fresh category-and-position reassociation permits limited recovery without trusting instance names or nominal height. All physical actions use the supplied public API, and uncertain execution ends the policy without further manipulation.

This policy addresses the reported carrying and release issues with a deeper nominal grasp target, additional closed-gripper settling, an optional intermediate transport waypoint, and a separate centered descent to the supplied release height. It avoids the previous fixed destination offsets and clears the basket before obtaining another scene. A bounded global assignment favors preserving existing category groups, while fresh spatial matching and limited source-region attempts support more than six cycles without treating frame-local names or nominal Z as physical verification. Recovery is restricted to explicit zero-execution path rejections; uncertain execution ends the policy without changing the gripper. These are proposed repairs, not a claim of successful sorting.

The policy addresses the reported failure modes with deeper nominal contact, additional gripper settling, elevated transport, centered vertical release, and vertical withdrawal. A bounded assignment search prioritizes fewer visible relocations before transport distance. Fresh RGB reassociation and a larger finite cycle bound replace persistent-name assumptions and the six-cycle limit. Explicit path rejection allows limited alternatives; uncertain execution ends the policy. No primitive result or visual heuristic is treated as proof of task success.
